meta.subtitle: Fourth kit: 20x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 (1.28 TB, symmetric 10+10 channels) - Tyrone MDA200A2N-224
meta.platform: Tyrone MDA200A2N-224 / 2x AMD EPYC 9135 (32C/64T, Zen 5 Turin)

executive_summary: Post-install revalidation of the fourth DIMM configuration fitted to server 172.16.11.132 today (Tyrone MDA200A2N-224, dual AMD EPYC 9135): 20x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 in a deliberate SYMMETRIC reduced population - channels E and K left vacant on both sockets (10+10), 1.28 TB total. Clean POST: all 20 modules train at full 5600 MT/s, ACPI BERT is empty and the BMC logged no memory events - the 4 vacant positions are by design, not failures (unlike the second kit's 2 mapped-out modules).

The 5-minute 100% burn held 1156 GB (92% of RAM) resident across 64 verify-mode workers and completed 1.40 billion verified operations with zero failures, zero OOM/swap; EDAC CE=0/UE=0, zero machine-checks, zero new SEL entries during the campaign; cores held full boost (peak 4343 MHz vs 4300 rated).

Bandwidth scales LINEARLY with channel count: 483.7 GB/s aggregate stream = 85% of the 24-DIMM figure (567.5 GB/s) on 83% of the channels - i.e. 102% of the linear 10-of-12 prediction; sysbench read/write land at 86%/84%. This is the controlled counter-example to this morning's asymmetric 22-DIMM kit, which kept 92% of the channels but lost 40% of the bandwidth. Symmetric de-population preserves the EPYC interleave; the configuration is qualified for production at its design point.

comparison.caption: Same server, same day, same tooling - symmetric 20-DIMM kit vs the 24-DIMM kit validated 30 minutes earlier.
comparison.notes: Bandwidth tracks channel count linearly when the layout stays symmetric: 483.7 GB/s is 85% of the 24-DIMM figure on 83% of the channels (sysbench read/write 86%/84%). Contrast with today's asymmetric 22-DIMM kit (Run 2): MORE DIMMs but only 348.6 GB/s (60%), because one socket ran 11 channels and broke the UMC interleave. Population symmetry, not module count, governs aggregate bandwidth on EPYC. Capacity at this design point: 1.28 TB.

sel_status: BMC SEL: 0 new entries during the campaign (355 before and after; last entry 10:23 UTC, pre-test boot). The 13 entries added during the swap session (342 -> 355) are PSU AC-loss/presence and chassis-intrusion artifacts at 10:10 (benign - AC pulled during physical work), clock syncs, and a clean 10:22/10:23 power-on. NO memory events - unlike the second kit, nothing was mapped out.
dmesg_status: Clean POST for this configuration: ACPI BERT is empty on the current boot (no error records ingested). During the campaign: 0 machine-check events, AMD EDAC CE=0/UE=0 on both controllers, core clocks 4100-4343 MHz under load, swap untouched, no OOM-killer activity.
findings: The 4 vacant positions are deliberate, not failures: channels E and K are skipped on BOTH sockets (symmetric 10+10), dmidecode simply reports no SPD in those slots, ACPI BERT is empty and the BMC logged zero 'Memory Device Disabled' events - the clean-POST signature, directly unlike the second kit whose 2 modules were mapped out with fatal DRAM storage errors.

Bandwidth scales linearly with channel count under symmetric population: 483.7 GB/s aggregate = 85.2% of the 24-DIMM baseline on 83.3% of the channels (102% of the linear prediction); DRAM-bound sysbench read 311.1 GB/s (86%) and write 171.7 GB/s (84%) agree. The EPYC UMC interleave is fully intact at 10+10.

Today's four runs now bracket the population-geometry rule: symmetric 24-DIMM ~570-580 GB/s; symmetric 20-DIMM ~484 GB/s (linear); asymmetric 22-DIMM only 348.6 GB/s - more modules, 28% less bandwidth than this 20-DIMM layout. Symmetry, not module count, governs aggregate bandwidth.

The 5-minute 100% burn is spotless: 1156 GB (92% of RAM) resident for the entire window, 1,396,932,249 verified operations with zero failures, zero OOM, swap untouched; EDAC CE=0/UE=0; zero machine-checks; zero new SEL entries during the campaign.
Single-thread and NUMA behavior nominal: 22.9 GB/s 1-thread memcpy, node0->node0 22.5 GiB/s vs node0->node1 14.0 GiB/s = 1.61x remote penalty (family norm).

Kit identity recorded for traceability: fourth distinct set today, zero serial overlap with all three prior kits. 19 modules from lot 80CE04254742Exxxxx plus ONE module from the older lot family (P1 CH-J, s/n 80CE04254642E03E0C) - mixed lot is acceptable (identical part number, speed, rank) but worth tracking in inventory. Full slot-by-slot map incl. the 4 vacant positions in the Hardware Inventory section.
recommendations: Configuration qualified at its design point: 20/20 modules trained, zero errors, linear-scaling bandwidth (~484 GB/s) and 1.28 TB capacity - cleared for production workloads sized to this envelope.
If full bandwidth/capacity is needed, populate the 4 vacant positions (CH E + K, both sockets): today's data predicts ~570-580 GB/s and 1.5 TB restored.

Adopt as a fleet rule: any reduced population MUST stay socket-symmetric (same channels on both sockets). Today's controlled comparison proves symmetric-20 out-delivers asymmetric-22 by 39% aggregate bandwidth.
Track the single older-lot module (P1 CH-J, s/n 80CE04254642E03E0C) in inventory; prefer uniform lots per server where stock allows.
Install rasdaemon and enable BIOS patrol scrub before production; optional 3-hour qualification soak (memtester near-full-residency + extended soak) before customer handover.
